title: Ramesh Verma v. M/s Star Developers
text: The complainant, Ramesh Verma, booked a flat with the opposite party, M/s Star Developers, in 2015 for Rs 45,00,000 and paid the full booking amount. The opposite party promised possession by 2018 but failed to deliver the flat. The complainant filed a complaint before NCDRC alleging deficiency in service and unfair trade practice. The NCDRC examined the builder-buyer agreement and found that the opposite party had no reasonable ground for the three-year delay. Deficiency in service by a builder who fails to deliver possession within the agreed time is well-established under consumer protection law. The NCDRC directs the opposite party to either deliver the flat or refund Rs 45,00,000 with 10% interest from 2018. Additionally, compensation of Rs 5,00,000 for mental agony and Rs 50,000 for litigation costs is awarded. The complainant is entitled to full relief as prayed.
